title: DOCKER-NAS-DEPLOYMENT: GHCR image + NAS-ready compose + measured resource floor + restore drill + corrected policy note
host: promaxgb10-83f1 (U1, aarch64, Ubuntu 24.04) - a permitted test host (decision #9)
gate_note: Decision #9 unchanged for our infrastructure. This card is for THIRD-PARTY customer hosts. Testing ran on U1, not on Don's NAS. No public GHCR push performed; the push+gated mechanism verified against a local OCI registry. Image digest and release-body wiring are recorded below.

image.architecture: linux/arm64 - build-verified and run-verified on U1
image.architecture_amd64: supported by the same arch-neutral Dockerfile; NOT build-verified in this run (QEMU-emulated cargo build segfaulted with exit 139 on the only available test host; retried with a dedicated builder, same result). Honest status: arm64 verified today; amd64 requires a native/CI amd64 runner for its first green build.
image.push_mechanism: release.sh --push-ghcr --ghcr-org <org> --digest-out <file>; preflight requires docker login with write:packages; repo digest written to digest-out for the release body. Verified end-to-end against 127.0.0.1:5000 (local OCI registry): tag -> push -> digest sha256:36f058... captured.
image.gate: First PUBLIC GHCR push waits for Don opening the surface (2026-10-27).

compose.pull_based: true (no build on the NAS; pulls ${OEP_IMAGE:-ghcr.io/isolith/oep-stack:0.1.0})
compose.explicit_port_bindings: 127.0.0.1 defaults via OEP_PDM_BIND/OEP_VIEWER_BIND/OEP_P2P_BIND/OEP_DOCS_BIND - LAN-off until operator publishes
compose.health_check_per_service: pdm /api/v1/health, viewer GET /, p2p /healthz, docs /healthz (5s interval)
compose.synology: Container Manager Project import reads the same compose; health shows in the project container list
compose.compose_config_validation: docker compose -f docker-compose.nas.yml config --quiet -> VALID; config --images -> 4x ghcr.io/isolith/oep-stack:0.1.0
compose.auth_on_by_default: true; pdm/viewer commands carry no --no-auth (SEC-AUTHZ-DEFAULT; P2T-04-AZ must not regress)

resource_floor_measured.method: docker stats --no-stream on the running stack (arm64 image 0.1.0, idle) on 2026-10-27, two samples
resource_floor_measured.cpu_idle_percent: pdm ~0.1-1%, viewer ~1.4-1.7%, docs ~0.8-2.2% (one vCPU or less combined)
resource_floor_measured.vault_volume_at_rest: pdm_data 16 KB with one seeded item + one blob + 2 audit entries
resource_floor_measured.stated_floor: 1 GB RAM free (whole stack idles < 30 MiB RSS; even 512 MB is ample), 1 GB free disk beyond the image day-1, 1 vCPU for the server component; CPU is dominated by on-demand batch-convert/render workers when actually used, which are one-shot binaries sized separately

security_posture.pdm_auth: ON by default; verified live: unauthenticated / wrong-role call -> 403 {"error":{"code":"forbidden"}} on POST items; items/audit/file 403 without identity headers
security_posture.lan_bind_guidance: set OEP_*_BIND to the NAS LAN IP behind a reverse proxy; never 0.0.0.0 on a WAN interface
tls_options: reverse proxy on the NAS (Synology Reverse Proxy etc.)
security_posture.air_gap_statement: air-gap holds ONLY when the host itself is isolated (no default route/DNS/registry); GHCR pull is NOT air-gap; air-gap install = signed offline bundle

backup_restore.what_to_back_up: named volume pdm_data (store.json + blobs/ + audit/) + .env/compose override; image is re-pullable
backup_restore.where_it_may_go: different physical disk/volume set or another NAS/offsite; NOT the same volume set that is the failure domain; for our infra NAS is never a target (vault-backup.sh guard refuses /mnt/nas*)
backup_restore.producer: scripts/backup/vault-backup.sh (sha256 manifest, blob name == content hash, self-verifying)
backup_restore.restore_proof: workstreams/delivery/deploy/proof/nas-restore-drill.log - PASS: fresh persist dir, fresh oep-pdm, health ok, item count 1, audit chain ok (2 entries), served file bytes hash bc7d34068dccaf7f701d696f22cd04cb9fc7dbf7760440121599b241f03bfd32 match the backup manifest
backup_restore.run_restore_check_after_changes: run scripts/backup/vault-restore-check.sh after any schema/migration/release change before the round-trip claim holds for the new train

steps: run scripts/backup/vault-restore-check.sh if release notes say a migration is required
upgrade_path.migrations: vault schema is versioned + forward-compatible (additive); oep-vault-migrate handles V5-era tree imports, not in-place downgrade; no destructive migration step on the NAS
upgrade_path.rollback: keep previous OEP_VERSION/OEP_IMAGE, up -d with it; named volume pdm_data is untouched by an image swap

docs_page.screenshot: docs-site/assets/images/07-nas-compose-equivalent.png (real U1 stack output rendered via headless Chrome; media-manifest.md records provenance)

policy_note: Decision #9 (NAS is repo/storage only, never host services, never a backup target) applies to OUR infrastructure and stands as written. This card is for customers hosting Isolith on THEIR OWN NAS/server; none of these instructions change our policy. Contracted at card top + nas-deployment.md section 0.
